Floral Shoppe cover art

Macintosh Plus’s album art: a Helios bust on a pink-and-black checkered floor beside a video still of the Twin Towers, with the title in green katakana.

Source
Wikipedia: Floral Shoppe
Creator
Macintosh Plus (Ramona Langley, also known as Vektroid)
Made
December 9, 2011 (digital release); 2012 cassette on Beer on the Rug
Style
Vaporwave (template; agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Nostalgic, ironic, surreal
Evidence
Inspected the 1200 × 1180 front J-card scan of the 2012 Beer on the Rug cassette (catalogue BOTR009) in the Cover Art Archive, in a scratchpad copy. Compared it with the 600 × 600 cover of the 2011 digital release in the same archive and with the current 1200 × 1200 Bandcamp art, a later variant in which the bust has no face and a compact-disc frame surrounds the image. Not stored.
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Released digitally on December 9, 2011, by Beer on the Rug. Wikipedia says it “established a blueprint for the genre” and that some albums, “including Floral Shoppe, depict the intact Twin Towers on their covers.” Wikipedia: Floral Shoppe; Wikipedia: Vaporwave.

The bust is a Roman copy of the head of Helios, which is itself public domain; the cover as a whole is a copyrighted composition. Wikipedia: Helios (statue)).

Observed

  • A cut-out marble head on a white plinth fills the left half of the square.
  • The background is flat salmon pink; a black-and-pink checkered floor recedes to a horizon at the lower right.
  • A blurred, orange-and-violet video still shows a city skyline with the Twin Towers over water.
  • The title is set in mint-green katakana and Latin capitals (MACプラス, フローラルの専門店) beside a green isometric cube icon and a green rule.
  • On the cassette card a Sega Saturn manual header and “compact disc 取扱説明書” sit at the top, and the spine runs a full rainbow gradient.

Why it belongs

Every later cliché is already here: statue, pink, checkerboard, Japanese title, degraded video, and a quoted consumer-electronics label. The composition is sparse and flat, closer to a desktop collage than a designed sleeve.

Borrow

Pair one cut-out object with one degraded video frame on a flat pastel ground, and add a perspective checkerboard in the lower third.
